400743.title: green mago
400743.addr: Plan O Building, 55-3 Bongeunsa-ro 68-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul
400743.overview: ‘Mago’ is Spanish for magician, and this group show gathers seven artists who bend the ordinary: Kwon Osang and Choi Wonkyo twist space and material, Lee Son and Ham Seongju scramble the real and the virtual, and Song Yeeun, Taniguchi Makoto and Ryu Jaesung undo the everyday systems and boundaries around us.

400744.title: Jin Minwook: Palimpsest
400744.overview: Jin Minwook collects landscapes on walks and copies out old poems and lines of literature, then weaves the two into new painted scenes. This solo show, running until 2 December, brings about twenty new works made after two years of walking the real places behind classic songs and stories, layering what is there now over what was written long ago, like a palimpsest.

400742.title: Chung Miok: In-between
400742.overview: Chung Miok starts from the familiar order of geometric form, borrowing from geometric abstraction, Minimalism and Op Art, then rearranges lines and planes in shifting colours, angles and layers so that flat surfaces seem to move and deepen as you look. Illusion and play turn a cool, rational language into a sensory one. Until 25 October.

400673.title: Colonies: Six Gardens, from the MMCA Art Bank Collection
400673.addr: 51 Wiryeseong-daero, Songpa-gu, Seoul (SOMA Museum of Art)
400673.price: ₩8,000; 50% off for groups of 20 or more

400890.title: Chae Sung-pil: Earth, Water and the Inscription of Time
400890.overview: Chae Sung-pil, known as the ‘artist of earth’, paints with soil dissolved in water, letting it flow, soak in, settle and dry so that gravity and time make the image. The show brings together his Anonymous Land, Reverie of the Earth and Portrait of Water series with the new Inscription works, whose vertical lines are not brushstrokes but traces left by earth, water and pigment, reading from a distance like ridges, valleys and rivers.
